Q: How to extract the correct server version from a MySQLDump? A:

Using any POSIX sed:

$ sed -En 's/^[- ]*Server version[[:space:]]+([0-9.]+-)?([0-9.]+)-.*/\2/p' file
10.11.8
10.3.34

I don't know if it matters to you or not but note that the only hard-coded words that script relies on being present are Server version, it doesn't rely on Maria or sql any other specific string bring present in the input just Server version, optionally preceded by blanks and/or minus signs, followed by spaces and then one or 2 --terminated version numbers, of which it prints the last one.

The above was run on this input file:

$ cat file
-- Server version   10.11.8-MariaDB-0ubuntu0.24.04.1
Server version 5.5.5-10.3.34-MariaDB-1:10.3.34+maria~focal-log

Q: Why aren't my benchmark results faster in Release compared to Debug? A:

The library functions have been compiled in Release mode. The compilation mode of your benchmark only matters for your own code, but does not impact the BCL string functions.

Q: typing.overload based on presence of keyword arguments A:

because the tool understands that kwargs might be empty, so the second overloading declaraiton also matches any call which fall into the first declaration - so the "overlapping" part.

if there is a way to declare statically that kwargs type (V2 above) must be a non-empty mapping, you have a chance of this working.

Unfortunatelly, it looks like Python static typing system lacks the capability for requiring something to be non-empty.

You can make your assertions inside the function code, by using a TypeGuard - check full info on PEP-647 - and if clauses - but without the elegance otherwise provided by overload declarations.

Q: Git is not working after macOS update ("xcrun: error: invalid active developer path (/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools") A:

If you use xcode then install it (~12GB)

xcode-select --install

Otherwise install latest command line tools (~500MB)

If stuck in install loop, run:

xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch

Q: Ai is the replacer of Web developer A:

If you think of a (web) developer as a human being writing computer code, Yes, that's something of the past. But humans will still be in control, someone has to tell the AI what you want the AI to build. And that's a skill on its own. Nearly all complaints about how AI fails in writing code, are actually about the human abilities in communication.

If you ask me for a coffee, you get black coffee. Not a latte, no sugar, just black. Why? That's how I drink it, that's my bias. If you want something different, you have to ask for it, YOU have to be specific.

Q: Xcode 26.2 Simulator download fails with DVTDownloadableErrorDomain Code 41 on macOS 26.1 A:

I had the same problem, due to Apple. I solve it by installing the 26.1 version.

Xcode -> Settings -> Components -> Other installed platforms

and choose iOS 26.1 Simulator
